[LUNI.4.1.2] **The baked base.** The seven SI base dimensions and their
canonical anchors are **primitive**: they are the coordinate axes of the
dimensional algebra, always in scope, and **non-redefinable** (a redeclaration is
`DS_VALIDATE_UNIT_IMPORT_COLLISION`). They are
not content an author imports — they are the basis everything else is
expressed over. The compiler pre-loads them as an implicit module
`units.core`, a `.ds` module of the library the compiler ships with
([LIMP.3.3.1]), read from there on every compilation:

| Dimension | Storage | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| `time` | int64 | nanosecond |
| `length` | float64 | meter |
| `mass` | float64 | kilogram |
| `temperature` | float64 | kelvin |
| `current` | float64 | ampere |
| `amount` | float64 | mole |
| `luminous_intensity` | float64 | candela |

`units.core` provides, for each base axis, the **anchor unit** above **and its
canonical short alias** — `nanosecond`/`ns`, `meter`/`m`, `kilogram`/`kg`,
`kelvin`/`K`, `ampere`/`A`, `mole`/`mol`, `candela`/`cd` — so the short-form base
literals resolve with no import.

**The `time` axis is baked in full**, at every scale [LUNI.10.2] declares on it —
`microsecond`/`us`, `millisecond`/`ms`, `second`/`s`, `minute`/`min`, `hour`/`h`
and `day`/`d`, alongside the `nanosecond`/`ns` anchor. It is the one axis whose
literals occupy **core grammar positions** — `cooldown`
([LGRA.6.6]), `after` ([LTAC.2.1]), `ttl`, `within`, `sliding` and `tumbling` — so
a duration literal is a term of the language rather than library content, and
making those productions depend on an import would leave them unwritable in a
file that imports nothing. `minute`, `hour` and `day` are baked with the rest
despite being non-SI: the set an author reaches for is the set that must be in
scope.

A program uses `5_kg`, `100_m`, `30_s` and `5_min` with **no import**. Scaled and
prefixed forms on the other six axes (`gram`, `kilometer`, …), affine units
(`celsius`), and the derived SI units (`watt`, `Hz`, …) are **not** baked: they
are declared in `units.si`, which builds on `units.core` and may not redeclare a
base axis. **Only these 7 axes are baked** — the six non-time axes at anchor plus
short alias, `time` at every scale [LUNI.10.2] declares — and everything else,
SI or otherwise, is earned by declaration.
